ns2:section.sectionText: This course will explore the dynamics of complex liquids, including particle and fiber suspensions and polymer solutions. A wide array of problems in chemical and biological engineering ranging from the petroleum to food industry rely on the processing of colloidal suspensions, surfactants, and polymer solutions, and it is of paramount importance to achieve a quantitative understanding of the flow properties of these materials. Emphasis is placed on the dynamics of complex liquids in non-equilibrium fluid flows, in situations far from thermal equilibrium. Foundational topics include stress in non-Brownian suspensions of spheres and fibers, developed from a first principle basis with relation to the stresslet. Brownian motion is considered, including Brownian particles and fibers, with development of stress in a Brownian suspension of rods. In the second part of the course, the dynamics of polymer solutions is considered, including stress in a dilute solution of polymers and development of appropriate constitutive equations (stress-strain rate relations). The classic Rouse model for multi-mode polymers is considered, followed by the Zimm model by inclusion of hydrodynamic interactions. Finally, semi-dilute unentangled and entangled polymers solutions are considered from the viewpoint of blob theory and scaling arguments, including recent developments in kinetic theories for semi-dilute solutions. The course will conclude with the basic aspects of entangled solutions and melts, with advanced topics including stress in branched polymer solutions and melts. Registration is limited to graduate students in chemical engineering, materials science, mechanical engineering, physics, chemistry, or related disciplines.
